prompt_en: A photographic scene of a fictional adult woman in a candid moment at an almost empty night roller rink beside the skate-return counter. Her face and hair are guided by the attached portrait: a short dark bob with fine parted bangs, a softly rounded facial contour, dark eyes and naturally pink lips. She glides left to right through her last slow lap, turning her head toward her rink-edge friend who is taking this photograph. A small, unguarded smile and the loose swing of her open slate satin blouson make the farewell feel close and spontaneous; an ivory fitted knit tank and dark tapered trousers belong naturally to the evening. Both quad-skate wheel sets meet the smooth floor, feet slightly staggered beneath softly bent knees, with her left arm held loosely outward for balance. The return counter and stacked rental skates mark where her glide is carrying her. Photograph her full body from nearby at chest height, with her face large enough to read and both skates inside the frame. The main impression is a compact-digital snapshot. Here near subjects receive direct frontal flash: her cheek and satin folds have crisp bright edges, with a short sharp floor shadow behind her skates and a dimmer rink. Slow-sync flash freezes one sharp body while a faint continuous exposure trail follows her moving sleeve and wheels toward screen left. Small cyan LEDs in the skate wheels leave short horizontal light streaks toward screen left behind the flash-frozen wheels; fixed rails and counter edges stay still. Dark image regions carry digital noise across the wall and shadowed sleeves and chest folds of her slate jacket. Dark image regions contain irregular brightness speckle, fine random light/dark pixels visibly scattered over those jacket gradients. Small colored speckles appear within dark image regions, including tiny green and magenta flecks in the same shaded jacket folds; speckles remain separate from large object colors. The speckle remains an image-plane artifact overlaying satin, rather than a woven pattern. Keep jacket shadows open enough to read this noisy texture. Noise fades into the bright face; skin texture, satin reflections and floor contact remain readable.
